n: Fornication. That is, idolatry. (Challoner) --- Down. Virgins used the stomacher, or (Haydock) fascia pectoralis, Isaias iii. 24. This chapter resembles the 16th. (Calmet)

Oolla and Ooliba. God calls the kingdom of Israel Oolla, which signifies their own habitation, because they separated themselves from his temple; and the kingdom of Juda Ooliba, which signifies his habitation in her, because of his temple among them in Jerusalem. (Challoner) --- The ten tribes first gave way to idolatry, and were more numerous. (Calmet) -- In Egypt the people were united, yet abandoned to idolatry in their youth, when they were only beginning to increase. Afterwards the ten tribes set up altars for themselves, at Dan and Bethel. (Worthington)

Assyrians. That is, the idols of the Assyrians: for all that is said in this chapter of the fornications of Israel and Juda, is to be understood in a spiritual sense of their disloyalty to the Lord, by worshipping strange gods. (Challoner) (Worthington) --- The Assyrians taught the worship of Baal, the high places, &c. The Egyptians also promoted their abominations. (Calmet)
Blue, or purple. This was reserved for the principal nobility.
Egypt. They always retained an affection for those idols, the calf, Adonis, &c.
Disgrace: satisfying their passions, ver. 29. (Calmet) --- Women. Having once lost all sense of decorum, they became more abandoned. (Haydock)
This; not chastisement, but dissolution.
Colours. She was enamoured at the account or picture of these people, without ever having seen them.
Messengers. Achaz invited the Assyrians, and imitated their altars, &c., 4 Kings xvi. 2., &c. (Calmet) --- The Chaldeans afterwards possessed the country. (Haydock)
Love. Literally, "of breasts," as Hebrew also signifies. Here it denotes the temples. (Haydock)
Remembering, or "causing to be remembered" by God, who seemed to have forgotten those ancient scenes of wickedness, chap. xxi. 24.
Asses. He means the Egyptians, (chap. xvi. 26.) in whom the kings of Juda trusted. (Calmet)
About. The Philistines, Ammonites, &c., shall join the Chaldeans, (Haydock) and Egypt shall desert the Jews in their greatest need. (Calmet)

Nobles. Protestants, "Pekod, and Shoah, and Roa:" (Haydock) which Junius takes to be the three great divisions of the empire. Others suppose they denote the dignities, though they occur not in Daniel. --- Captains. Hebrew, "Phachat, and Saganim, (ver. 6, 12.) and Schalischim;" officers mentioned [in] Exodus xiv. 7., and 2 Kings xxiii. 8. --- Renowned, called to the assemblies and councils of the prince, Numbers i. 16. (Calmet) --- Horsemen. Protestants, "all of them riding upon horses." (Haydock)
Judgments, at Reblatha, 4 Kings xxv. 6.

Jealousy, the most violent of passions. (Calmet) --- So the Chaldeans are styled, as Assur is the rod, Isaias x. 5. (Worthington) --- Ears, the punishment of adulteresses: both king and priests suffer. (St. Jerome) --- Thus the captives were probably treated. (Calmet) See Seneca, Ira. iii. 20. --- Fire, by Ismahel, chap. xix. 14.
Glory; vanity, or of the temple, chap. xvi. 17., and Osee ii. 4.
Cup. Thou shalt be punished like Samaria, dreadfully, 4 Kings xvii. 4. (Calmet)
Fragments, as drunkards sometimes bite (Haydock) the cup in their rage. --- Rend. What had been the occasion of thy fall: (Calmet) pectori planxi. (Ovid, ep. 5.)
Deeds. He is thus admonished to condemn them; (chap. xx. 4.) as times and places tended to aggravate their crimes, ver. 39. (Worthington)
Paint, with antimony. (Septuagint) See 4 Kings ix. 3.
Bed: it seems at table, Amos ii. 8., and Tobias ii. 3. --- Ointment; using them for thyself, or presenting them to idols, Exodus xxx. 23, 33. (Calmet)

And that. Protestants, "Sabeans (marginal note and Septuagint, drunkards) from," &c. Any were admitted (Haydock) to the priesthood and to her favours, even the most rustic and deformed, 3 Kings xii. 32.
Just, compared with the Jews, whom they shall chastise. (Calmet)
Stones, like adulteresses, chap. xvi. 38., and Leviticus xx. 10. (Haydock) --- Let the walls be demolished. (Calmet)

f: Commentary on Ezekiel

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother, and they committed fornication in Egypt; in their youth they committed fornication: there their breasts were subdued, and the teats of their puberty were broken (or, as is contained in the Seventy, there their breasts fell, and there they were deflowered). Their names were Oholah the greater (or the elder) and Oholibah her sister; and I had them (or they became mine) and they bore sons and daughters: and their names were Samaria Oholah and Jerusalem Oholibah. Oholah therefore committed fornication over me; and she went mad (or went off) after her lovers, after the Assyrians, who drew near to her, clothed in hyacinth, princes and magistrates, young men of desire (or chosen), all horsemen, riders of horses. And she bestowed her fornications upon them, the chosen sons of the Assyrians, all of them; and in the uncleannesses (or inventions) of all those over whom she went mad she was polluted. Moreover she did not abandon her fornications either, which she had had in Egypt; for they too had slept with her in her youth, and had broken the breasts of her puberty (or and they themselves had deflowered her), and had poured out their fornication upon her. Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the sons of Asshur, over whose lust she went mad; they uncovered her shame, they took her sons and daughters, and they killed her herself with the sword; and they became notorious women (or she became a byword among women), and they executed judgments (or vengeances) upon her. That the twelve tribes of Israel, which were joined together in Egypt, were afterwards divided into two and ten tribes and called Judah and Israel, the scripture of Kings and of Παραλιπόμενον [Chronicles] testifies. Over Judah there reigned, from the stock of David, Rehoboam son of Solomon, in Jerusalem, where the temple was, and the priests, and a great part of the tribe of Levi; but over the ten tribes, in Samaria, Jeroboam son of Nebat, of the tribe of Ephraim and of Joseph; of which Samaria is now called 'Oolla' [Oholah], which in our language sounds 'tabernacle', but Jerusalem 'Ooliba' [Oholibah], that is, 'my tabernacle in her'; for indeed among the ten tribes too there was a tabernacle, not of God but of idols: for Jeroboam, in order to turn the people away from the worship of God, had set up golden calves in Dan and Bethel. Let us speak, then, of each. These two women, Samaria and Jerusalem, were daughters of one mother, begotten of the stock of Israel, and they committed fornication in Egypt in their youth; for they would not, when led out of Egypt, have received on Mount Sinai the law forbidding them to venerate idols, had they not venerated the Egyptian monstrosities in Egypt —but the mother of both can be the Hittite, of whom we read above: Your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite; and also when it is said: 'Let each one cast away the abominations of Egypt from his eyes', this signifies that Israel served idols in Egypt and that there the breasts of its virginity fell, or were broken — ; and Samaria is called the greater and the elder, either because of the multitude of the ten tribes, or because, after the death of Moses, Joshua son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, presided over the people, from which tribe too, we read, Jeroboam came, who split them off from the house of David. And God had them, or they became his, when they groaned under the works of Egypt, slaving before that at clay and brick; and afterwards they bore him sons and daughters, whether in the wilderness or in the land of promise.
Commentary on Ezekiel

According to the ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense], we have discussed more fully in the prophet Hosea what Joseph, Ephraim, Samaria, Jezreel and Israel signify, and how they are opposed to the house of David and to Jerusalem, which signifies the Church — of whom Psalm 77 (78) also sounds: The sons of Ephraim, bending and shooting the bow, turned back in the day of battle, and again: He rejected the tabernacle of Joseph and chose the tribe of Judah; for the Lord chose the house of confession, the Church, and rejected the tabernacle of 'Joseph', which means 'increase'; and they, setting aside the law of God, added golden calves of their own worship —; and she is called 'Oolla', that is, 'tabernacle', not of God but of error and of demons; and the sister, greater and elder because of her multitude and her captivity by the Assyrians, committed fornication against God, because she abandoned the truth of the faith and went mad after the princes of the heretics, her lovers, who were clothed in hyacinth, promising themselves lofty and heavenly things, and riders, of whom it is said: Some in chariots and some on horses, chosen sons of the Assyrians, and leaders and magistrates, who promise themselves knowledge and eloquence; and she did this because the same fornications that she had had in Egypt, that is, before she believed and while she was still living in the world, she practiced in heresy too; and she was deflowered by Assyrian men, who persevere in malice, or by avengers — for our adversary the devil is himself the enemy and the avenger — ; they broke the breasts of Samaria, and destroyed the virginity which she had had in the Church; therefore she was handed over to her lovers, according to the Apostle, who writes: I delivered them to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme, and he delivered them for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved; they uncovered the shame of wretched Samaria, and displayed all her foulness; and her sons and daughters, who were begotten of her, both those endowed with knowledge and the simple and unskilled, they led captive; and they killed her herself with the spiritual sword; and they are celebrated, in the bad sense, in the talk of the whole world; and they become notorious among all the doctrines of the world, so that her foulness is punished as an example to all women.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And first Oholah, that is, Samaria, committed fornication over God, when she went mad after the Assyrians, who were clothed in hyacinth, and not just anyone of the people but leaders and magistrates, not men worn out with age but all young men, chosen horsemen, whose idols she followed and from whom, against the command of God, she requested help; and they came and polluted her, so that she did not abandon whatever she had done in her youth in Egypt —for the Egyptians too had lain with her in her youth, whose images she venerated, and there she was deflowered and her breasts were broken; and so great was the abundance of fornication that they are said not to have committed fornication with her but to have poured out their fornication —.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Therefore she was handed over to her lovers themselves, Pul and Tiglath-pileser and Shalmaneser, after whose lust she went mad; and they themselves uncovered her shame — τροπολογικῶς [tropologically], as of a harlot woman; but the uncovering of a city is captivity — ; and they led their sons and daughters captive and slaughtered her herself with the sword, so that she was butchered as an example to all women —and is celebrated, in the bad sense, in the talk of all of them — ; and they executed judgments and vengeances upon her —so as to leave nothing of safety in her, but the ten tribes are held in captivity to this day in the mountains and cities of the Medes to which they were transported —.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And when her sister Oholibah had seen this, she went mad with lust more than she, and shamelessly offered her fornication, beyond the fornication of her sister, to the sons of the Assyrians: to leaders and magistrates coming to her, clothed in varied garments (or costly), to horsemen who rode upon horses, and to youths all of outstanding form. And I saw that she was polluted: one way for both; and she increased her fornications. And when she had seen men painted on the wall, images of the Chaldeans expressed in colors, with their loins girded with belts, and dyed tiaras on their heads, with the appearance of all leaders (or of all the tristatae), in the likeness of the sons of Babylon and of the land of the Chaldeans in which they were born, she went mad over them with the lust of her eyes, and sent messengers to them in Chaldea. And when the sons of Babylon had come to her, to the bed of breasts (or of those turning aside), they polluted her with their debaucheries; and she was polluted by them, and her soul was sated (or withdrew) from them. And she laid bare her fornications, and uncovered her shame; and my soul withdrew from her, as my soul had withdrawn from her sister. For she multiplied her fornications, remembering the days of her youth in which she committed fornication in the land of Egypt; and she went mad with lust over the bedding of those whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses (or whose private parts are like the private parts of horses). And you revisited the wickedness of your youth, when your breasts were subdued in Egypt, and the teats of your puberty were broken. According to the letter the interpretation is easy: that Oholibah —that is, Jerusalem, in which was the tabernacle of God —, seeing the blows dealt to her sister, was not warned by the example to draw back her foot from error, but increased her sister's fornication —for that one fabricated idols once, and outside, in Dan and Bethel; but this one often, on the high places and in the temple of God, worshiped the statue of Baal and committed fornication with the Assyrians; for the idol Baal, or Bel, and, to speak more plainly, Belis, the religion of the Assyrians, was consecrated by Ninus son of Belus in honor of his father — ; and she shamelessly offered her fornication to the Assyrians, to leaders and magistrates who were clothed in varied and many-colored garments, to horsemen and youths all of outstanding form, so that the fornication of both sisters became one.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Moreover, according to tropology the understanding is difficult: how the Church can surpass heretical lust; unless perhaps we can say this, that the servant who knows the will of his master and does not do it will be beaten with many blows, and that heretics commit abominations outside and perish by shipwreck outside the ark of Noah, while churchmen, if, though following the true faith, they imitate Assyrian and Chaldean vices and follow the many-colored images of sins, deserve greater torments — or do we not send messengers to the 'Chaldeans', which means 'as it were demons', when we lay open and offer them the breasts to be broken in the bosom, where the lodging of the mind is, and, sated with pleasures, pass from some women to others; and desire not so much fornication as a number of harlots; and come to such madness that, after long years of the Lord's service, we return to Egypt and do the things we did in the world before we received the name of the faith? —.
Commentary on Ezekiel

But Jerusalem increased her fornications in this, that, seeing on the walls images of the Chaldeans, she went mad with lust and, deceived by their form and dress, sent messengers to them requesting help, and they came and polluted her.
Commentary on Ezekiel
And because pleasure is not perpetual but quickly brings satiety, polluted and sated with them, she withdrew from their covenant.
Commentary on Ezekiel

'Therefore I too, seeing her foul deeds and fornications made public to all, withdrew from her, so that she who had outdone her sister's crimes might also surpass her sister in the magnitude of her punishments'.
Commentary on Ezekiel

She was of such wantonness that she committed all the errors of her youth at an age already more mature, and pursued the Egyptian vices in her lust for the Chaldeans too; for she once went mad in her bedding with the Egyptians, whose flesh is in the likeness of asses, with so copious an issue of seed, or private parts so huge, that they surpass the deformity of horses.
Commentary on Ezekiel

'Nor did the wickedness of her youth cease; rather, she went back to it after she became mine, so that both in the wilderness and in the land of promise she sighed for the old lust in which she was deflowered and her breasts were broken and all her virginal beauty perished'.
Commentary on Ezekiel

All of this is said under the metaphor of an adulteress, disfigured because of her adultery, so that she may no longer glory in her comeliness but blush in the hideousness which she has merited by the magnitude of her pleasures. Whatever is said τροπικῶς [figuratively] of Jerusalem can also be referred to the soul, which, joined by its virtues to the embrace of God, afterwards turned adulteress to vices and withdrew from him, and, all her crimes being laid open, was stripped and disfigured and shown to all, so that she may at some time desist from her wickedness; and may not glory in the dignity of her name, but, from her consciousness of evil and her remembrance of Egypt, may not dare any longer to lift her eyes to heaven; whence too her nose is cut off and her ears are amputated, because she had turned the odor of good fragrance into stench and had heard the judgment of blood; and this we understand not only of smell and hearing but of sight too, of which Samson and Zedekiah are deprived because they had abused it; God also makes deaf and mute, so that their tongue may not pass through to the earth; and all touch is taken away in those who have utterly lost life. And these things will happen so that all things may be purged by fire, and the fornication of Egypt may perish, and she may no longer be able to raise her eyes to evils.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will stir up all your lovers against you, with whom your soul was sated; and I will gather them against you round about, the sons of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, nobles and tyrants and princes, all the sons of the Assyrians, youths of outstanding form, all the leaders and magistrates, princes of princes, and renowned riders of horses; and they will come upon you equipped with chariot and wheel, a multitude of peoples: with breastplate and shield and helmet they will be armed against you on every side, and I will set judgment before them, and they will judge you with their judgments. And I will set my jealousy in you, which they exercise with you in fury: they will cut off your nose and your ears, and what remains they will cut down with the sword; they themselves will take your sons and your daughters, and your last will be devoured by fire. And they will strip you of your garments, and take away the vessels of your glory; and they will make your wickedness rest from you, and your fornication from the land of Egypt, and you will not lift up your eyes to them, and you will not remember Egypt any more. (LXX: "Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will stir up your lovers against you, from whom your soul withdrew; and I will bring them against you round about, the sons of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, Facud and Sue and Cue, and all the sons of the Assyrians with them, chosen youths, all leaders and magistrates, τριστάτας [tristatae, high officers], and renowned men riding on horses; all will come upon you from the north, chariots and wheels with a multitude of peoples: shields and targes, and they will set a guard upon you round about, and I will set judgment before their face, and they will judge you with their judgments. And I will set my jealousy in you, and they will deal with you in the wrath of fury: they will take away your nose and your ears, and your remnant they will cast down with the sword; they themselves will take your sons and your daughters, and fire will devour your residue. And they will strip you of your garment, and take up the vessels of your boasting; and they will turn away your impieties from you, and your fornication from the land of Egypt, and you will not raise your eyes to them, and you will not remember Egypt any more.") 'Because you remembered the flesh of the Egyptians and imitated the foulness of an unclean nation which venerates images of all the beasts, therefore I will bring against you your lovers, sated with whose embrace you withdrew from their covenant, so that, as great as your love had been before, into so great a hatred you might be turned.
Commentary on Ezekiel

The sons, I say, of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, nobles, tyrants and princes — in place of which the Hebrew has 'facud' and 'sue' and 'cue', which many understand as nations of the east, since we find names of this kind neither in the volume of Kings nor in Chronicles, nor even in Jeremiah, which describe the captivity of Jerusalem, nor in any other place of holy scripture; nor is it surprising if the Seventy set down the Hebrew names themselves, since Symmachus too and Theodotion agree in the same words — ; all', he says, 'the Assyrians, horsemen and youths of outstanding form, leaders and magistrates — or τριστάτας, which we have translated 'princes of princes', of whom we also read in Exodus: Chosen riders, τριστάτας, in place of which Latin simplicity translated 'ternos stratores' [grooms by threes]; and 'tristatae' is the name among the Hebrews for the second rank after the royal dignity, of whom it is written: Yet he did not attain to the first three; they were princes of the cavalry and the infantry and of the tributes, whom we call magistrates of both services and prefects of the grain office — ; all', he says, 'in chariots and on horses, armed with breastplate, helmet and shield, will besiege you, and that round about; and I will give them judgment, so that you may be judged by those whom you had left and whose pact you had made void; and they will judge you with their judgments as an adulteress; and I will set', he says, 'my jealousy in you, which they exercise with you in fury — for my jealousy over faith not kept is present even among enemies — : your nose', he says, 'and your ears they will cut off — as of an adulteress caught in debauchery — so that, disfigured, you may cease to please — for just as in the face all the beauty of the countenance consists in the comeliness of the nostrils and in the ears, from which in women pearls and gems hang down, so the dignity of the king and of the judges, which is signified in the face and the ears, will be cut off by their sword — ; they themselves will take your sons and your daughters — yours, he says, and yours, not mine and mine, because they were begotten of adultery —, and the rest will be devoured by fire; and they will strip', he says, 'you of your garments, with which I had adorned you, and of the vessels of your glory, of gold and silver, which I had granted you for the ceremonies of the temple — of which it is written: I gave them gold and silver, and they made them for Baal — ; and I will do all these things so that, your beauty lost and your bewitching face disfigured, your wickedness may at last rest, and the fornication which you learned and practiced in Egypt, so that, after you have lost your nose and ears, you may by no means dare to lift your eyes to the Chaldeans and show your hideousness to your former lovers; nor may you any longer remember the lust of the Egyptians, in the size of whose flesh you delighted'.
Commentary on Ezekiel

For thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will deliver you into the hands of those whom you hated, into the hands with which your soul was sated, and they will deal with you in hatred, and take away all your labors, and leave you naked and full of disgrace. Your wickedness and your fornications have done these things to you, because you committed fornication after the nations, among whom you were polluted in their idols. You walked in the way of your sister, and I will give her cup into your hand. Thus says the Lord God: You will drink the cup of your sister, deep and wide — you will be for derision and for scorn: you who are most capacious, you will be filled with drunkenness and sorrow! —, and the cup of grief and sadness, the cup of your sister Samaria; and you will drink it and drain it to the dregs; and you will devour its fragments, and you will tear your breasts (or, as the Seventy translated, I will take away her feasts and new moons), for I have spoken, says the Lord. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have forgotten me, and cast me behind your body, you too bear your wickedness and your fornications. It is profitable for Jerusalem too to have enmity against the Assyrians and Chaldeans and by no means to remember Egypt, but to be delivered into the hands of those who hated her, to be punished; and she is not delivered to them before her soul has been sated with them, so that, after she has repented of her old sins, she may then be purged by punishments, and lose all the labors which she acquired by the harlot's art, and see her nakedness and disgrace, and know that it was not the Lord who did all these things to her but her own fornications, by which she committed fornication among the nations, which he enumerated above, so as to worship their images.
Commentary on Ezekiel

'In the ways', he says, 'of your sister Samaria you walked; therefore you must drink the cup of her whose sins you followed — and that a cup is often taken for punishments and torments, there are many examples, among which is this: A cup in the hand of the Lord, full of pure wine, mixed. And he has tilted it from this; yet its dregs are not emptied: all the sinners of the earth shall drink; and in Isaiah it is called 'the cup of ruin' and 'the draught of fury'; and God speaks to Jeremiah, saying: Take the cup of pure wine from my hand, and you shall give drink to all the nations to which I shall send you; and they shall drink and vomit, and go mad; for just as certain cathartics are given so that the noxious humor that is in bodies may be purged out, so the Lord too gives a most undiluted cup of torments, to take away from sinners whatever there is of gall and bitterness and restore them to their former health — ; and the cup itself will be deep and wide: deep in the magnitude of the punishments, wide in the length of the captivity; but when', he says, 'you have been made drunk and seized by sorrow, and have drunk the cup to the dregs and drained it to such a degree that you devour even the fragments of the cup itself, then you will be weary of your former fornication and will tear the breasts which had been broken in Egypt and which were subdued and crushed by your lovers — or I will take away all your feasts and new moons, so that in place of solemnity and gladness you may have eternal lamentation and grief —.
Commentary on Ezekiel

This that is said: And you will drink to the dregs; and you will devour its fragments, can be understood meaningfully of Jerusalem, which drank the cup of her sister Samaria last, and drained, as it were, the dregs of her torments to the bottom.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Since, therefore, you have done these things and forgotten me and cast me behind your body —or backward, because of the vices of the body, or behind the genitals, by which the foulness of turpitude is indicated —, therefore bear your wickedness and your impiety — that is, the punishments which you have merited by your impiety and crimes —'.
Commentary on Ezekiel

All these things were said τροπικῶς [figuratively] and under the type of adulteresses against Samaria and Jerusalem: that, delivered to the Assyrians and Chaldeans, they were led into captivity and their cities were burned up in fire, and the peoples were killed who had venerated the images of demons in place of God. These things can also be understood of the time after the coming of Christ: that righteous men from the peoples of the Gentiles, they themselves, judge the Samaritans and the Jews by comparison with themselves and deliver them to be devoured, those to whom the Lord had said: Your house will be left to you desolate, and: When you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, know that its desolation draws near; for to this day they are adulteresses and are crushed by the stones of the whole world, because they sent messengers to those who were far off and could not say: I am the Lord who draws near, and not from afar, says the Lord; and they prepared themselves for their lovers, the demons, and all the adornment and finery which they had received from God as a natural good they turned into the worship of demons, and their works and comeliness, which we understand in the bracelets and the diadem, they offered to their adulterous lovers; and their punishment is a fear to the Gentiles, or rather to those of the Gentiles who have believed, lest they suffer the like if they do what Samaria and Jerusalem did. From them impieties will be taken away then, when they have received their crimes and have taken away from their eyes the veil that is placed before the face of Moses, so that they may know that he himself is the Lord Jesus Christ, whom they denied to be the Son of God.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And the Lord spoke to me, saying: Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah, and declare to them their crimes (or iniquities)? For they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands, and they have committed fornication with their idols (or inventions); moreover their sons too, whom they had borne to me, they offered to them to be devoured (or they led through the fire). But this too they did to me: they polluted my sanctuary on that day, and profaned my sabbaths. And when they sacrificed their sons to their idols, and entered my sanctuary on that day to pollute it, these things too they did in the midst of my house. They sent to men coming from afar, to whom they had sent a messenger; and so, behold, they came. For them you washed yourself (or when they had come, at once you bathed), and painted round your eyes with stibium, and adorned yourself with womanly finery; you sat on a beautiful couch, and a table was adorned before you; my incense and my ointment (or oil) you set upon it. And the voice of an exulting multitude was in her (or and with a composed voice she leapt about), and among the men, indeed, multitudes of people were brought and came from the desert (or drunk from the desert); they put bracelets on their hands and most beautiful crowns on their heads. And I said to her who is worn down in adultery: Now she too will commit fornication in her fornication. And they went in to her as to a harlot woman; so they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah, wicked women (or to work iniquity). Righteous men, then, are they; these will judge them with the judgment of adulteresses and the judgment of those who shed blood, because they have committed adultery and blood is on their hands. For thus says the Lord God: Bring a multitude against them, and deliver them to tumult and to plunder; and let them be stoned with the stones of the peoples, and pierced with their swords; they will kill their sons and daughters, and burn their houses with fire. And I will remove wickedness (or impiety) from the land, and all women will learn not to act according to their wickedness (or impiety); and they will lay your wickedness (or impiety) upon you, and you will bear the sins of your idols, and you will know that I am the Lord God. As I have often pointed out, the small points in which the edition of the Seventy differs from the Hebrew I have joined on at the side, providing against the reader's distaste. Now it followed that he who had described the adulteries of Samaria and Jerusalem separately should announce their punishments together. And everything is said as to adulteresses, and, after a ἀνακεφαλαιῶσι [recapitulation] has been made, their crimes are briefly set forth, so that, rightly, according to the command of the law, the stoning of the people may follow upon the adulteresses. 'Since, therefore, they are adulteresses, pronounce a just sentence; for they have committed adultery with idols, and blood is on their hands, the blood, namely, of those whom they sacrificed to idols, so as to consecrate to demons the sons whom they had borne to me; nor did they do this outside, and on the mountains and in the groves, as they had often been accustomed to do, but at the last they polluted my temple, so as to set the statue of Baal in it; and they profaned my sabbaths, so that the religion neither of place nor of time was kept among them.
Commentary on Ezekiel

But neither were they content only with present adulteries, nor did it suffice them that, after sacrificing my sons, they made them their idols' or the demons', but, wanton also in foreign pleasures, they venerated the images of the Assyrians and Chaldeans. And when these had come, Oholibah, Jerusalem, you fulfilled for them the whole bearing of an adulteress: you washed your body, smeared your eyes with stibium, put on womanly adornment, sat on a couch prepared for lust, set out feasts with which to restore the strength of your lovers, broken by lust; my incense and ointment — which I had ordered to be made specially for me, and that soul to be exterminated from the people which wished to make it for private uses — you offered to idols, so as to gather a throng of peoples, or sang with every kind of musician, so as to please your lovers not only by sight but by hearing and smell and all the senses; and they came to you drunk, not with any urbane elegance, but from the desert and the wilderness, displaying the bearing of rustics and brigands. And into such madness of pleasures did you burn, O most wicked sisters, that you placed your bracelets and hair-ornaments upon the hands and heads of your lovers, or upon yourselves, so that, full of adornment, you might be disgraced.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Wherefore I said to her, whether to Jerusalem or to Samaria or to both: So have you worn down your brow that you are by no means polluted in secret, nor do you heed the gaze either of a husband or of men, but like harlots you are prostituted publicly; they went in to you as to harlots, vying with one another in their desire to pollute you.
Commentary on Ezekiel

I will therefore deliver you for punishment to those to whom you delivered yourselves of your own accord for defilement; for they are righteous men in this, that at my command they torment the adulteress and parricide.
Commentary on Ezekiel

For thus says the Lord God: By the warning of your voice, O prophet, gather against them a multitude of peoples, and first let all their substance be plundered; then let them be stoned and pierced with swords; and let their sons and daughters be slaughtered, and their houses burn.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And all these things will be done so that impiety may be removed from the land, and all women and all provinces may learn from their punishments to avoid the like, so that, after you have received what you deserve and have borne the crimes of your idols, you may then know that I am the Lord'.

n: Month; January 30, the year of the world 3414. (Usher) --- Ezechiel was then in Mesopotamia, and when the news of the siege commencing on that very day, should arrive; it would make a great impression upon the people, so that they would have confidence in him, (Calmet) as the certainty of the prediction would appear, 4 Kings xxv. 1. (Worthington)

Pot, to denote Jerusalem: the flesh boiled and consumed in the fire with the bones, would shew the future dismal condition of its chiefs and inhabitants. (Haydock) --- The hardened Jews turned such things to ridicule, chap. xi. 3.

Choice. Hebrew, "the choice of the bones," or the finest pieces separated from the bones, as the Septuagint and the sequel seem to require. (Calmet) --- The bones might serve to burn, ver. 5. (Haydock) See St. Jerome. (Vatable, &c.) (Calmet)
The, &c. Literally, "its boiling has grown hot;" the citizens suffer terribly. --- Bones. Hebrew hatsamim, (Haydock) may denote the more solid meat.

Rust: the inveterate malice of the city, ver. 12. --- Upon it. Hurl the pieces of meat out of the pot, without any choice. (Calmet) --- All the people shall feel my indignation, the rich as well as the poor, ver. 13. (Haydock)

She hath. Septuagint, "I have let it corrupt upon. I have not," &c., (ver. 8.; Haydock) as if God spoke. The Jews had committed murder without fear. They had naturally a horror for blood, and the law ordered even that of beasts to be covered, Leviticus xvii. 13. Now innocent blood cries for vengeance, Genesis iv. 10. The punishment shall be as visible as the crime, ver. 8.
And the. Hebrew, "put in the seasoning and the bones," &c.

Thy. Hebrew, "In thy crime there is design," or malice. This rendered the Jews so hateful (Calmet) and irreclaimable. (Haydock) --- God had given them abundant instructions (Calmet) and graces; but all was contemned. (Haydock) --- When the fire of tribulation does not amend sinners, they are sentenced to hell fire. (Worthington)

Stroke; pestilence, or sudden death. This would make the loss of a dear wife still more afflicting. Yet such distress will fall upon the whole nation, (Calmet) and misery shall increase so much, that a private loss will be almost forgotten. (Haydock) --- Curæ leves loquuntur, graviores silent. (Seneca, Troad.) --- When a loss is foreseen, it is more easily borne. Private calamities sink in public ones. (Worthington)

Silence, for such manifold calamities, if thou canst screen thyself from the enemy, who will otherwise take offence, as he has brought them on. (Haydock) --- Dead. Priests were allowed to mourn only for father or mother, and their unmarried brothers and sisters, Leviticus xxi. 1. Ezechiel (xliv. 25.) adds, Son and daughter. Many think the wife must also be understood, as she is nearer than a brother. The reasons for these prohibitions did not then subsist, as no sacrifice could be offered in Chaldea; and therefore God here specifies what the prophet was not to do, (Calmet) though lawful on other occasions. (Sanctius) --- Tire. Literally, "crown," bandage, (Calmet) or parchment, on which parts of the law were written. Septuagint, "Let (Roman edition adds, not) the hair of thy head be curled (or ruffed; sumpeplegmenon) upon thee." (Haydock) --- It was usually cut in mourning. (St. Jerome) --- Feet. They were bare, at funerals, and in times of sorrow, 2 Kings xv. 30. --- Face, like David. Hebrew, "the upper lip," which mourners and lepers covered, Leviticus xiii. 45. (Calmet) --- Mourners. Feasts were prepared by the relations, (Josephus, Jewish Wars ii. 1.) and friends sent some food, but no delicacies, to those who mourned, Leviticus v. 9.
Profane, or esteem it no more, (Haydock) but abandon it to the Gentiles. (Calmet) --- Feareth to lose; or on which it rests, ver. 25. (Haydock)
No more, if thou darest to speak before the Chaldeans, ver. 17. Reserve thy tears and lamentations for that time. (Calmet)

f: Commentary on Ezekiel

And the word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, saying: Son of man, write down for yourself the name of this day, on which the king of Babylon has been made strong against Jerusalem today. And you shall speak by a proverb a parable to the provoking house, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Set on the pot; set it on, I say, and put water into it. Heap its pieces into it, every good part, the thigh and the shoulder, choice pieces and full of bones; take the fattest of the flock, and arrange also piles of bones under it. Its cooking has boiled up, and its bones have been boiled through in the midst of it. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Woe to the city of bloods, to the pot whose rust is in it, and its rust has not gone out of it. Piece by piece, and by its pieces, cast it out; the lot has not fallen upon it, for its blood is in the midst of it; upon a most clear rock she poured it out; she did not pour it out upon the ground, so that it could be covered with dust: that I might bring my indignation upon her and avenge with vengeance, I have set her blood upon the most clear rock, so that it should not be covered. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Woe to the city of bloods, whose pyre I will make great. Heap up the bones, which I will set alight with fire; the flesh shall be consumed, and the whole composition shall be boiled down, and the bones shall waste away. Set it also empty upon the live coals, that it may grow hot, and its bronze may melt, and its defilement may be melted down in its midst, and its rust may be consumed. With much labor there has been sweating, and its excessive rust has not gone out of it, not even through fire. Your uncleanness is execrable, because I wished to cleanse you, and you were not cleansed of your filth; but neither will you be cleansed before I make my indignation rest upon you. I the Lord have spoken; it comes, and I will do it: I will not pass over, nor spare, nor be appeased. According to your ways and according to your devices I have judged you, says the Lord. (LXX: "And the word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, saying: Son of man, write down for yourself the day from this day on which the king of Babylon set himself firmly over Jerusalem from this present day. And speak a parable to the exasperating house, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Set on the cauldron, and pour water upon it. And put into it the divisions, every good cut, the leg and the shoulder, taken from choice cattle, with the flesh separated from the bones; and burn the bones beneath them. It has boiled, it has boiled, and its bones have been boiled out in the midst of it. Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: O city of bloods, cauldron in which there is rust in it, and the rust has not gone out of it. By its parts it has brought it out; the lot has not fallen upon it, because its blood is in the midst of it; upon a most smooth rock I have set it; I did not pour it out upon the ground, so that it should be covered with earth: that fury might go up to the avenging of vengeance, I have set her blood upon the most clear rock, so that it should not be covered. Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: Woe to the city of bloods, and I will make the firebrand great and I will multiply the wood and I will kindle the fire, that the flesh may waste away and the broth be diminished, and the bones be burned up and it stand upon its coals. It has been kindled that it may be burned out, and its bronze be roasted, and its uncleanness be burned up in its midst, and its rust fail. The rust shall be humbled, and its abundant rust shall not go out of it; its rust shall be put to confusion. Your uncleanness is 'zemma', because you were defiled, and you have not been cleansed of your uncleanness. And what will it be if you are not cleansed any more, until I fulfil my fury upon you? I the Lord have spoken; and it will come, and I will do it: I will not delay, nor have mercy, nor be entreated. According to your ways and according to your devices I will judge you, says Adonai the Lord." — Most of these were added from Theodotion, and so was the Hebrew word 'zemma', for which we translated 'execrable uncleanness'; and this too was added by them, which is not found in the Hebrew and must be marked beforehand with an obelus: ÷ Therefore I judge you according to your blood, and according to your thoughts I will judge you, unclean and notorious and excessive in provoking. ⁚) Let us speak, then, about each point. In the ninth year of the captivity of King Jehoiakim — for he began to prophesy in the fifth —, and in the tenth month of the same ninth year, on the tenth day of the tenth month, the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel the prophet, who was placed in the regions of Babylon, and said to him: 'Son of man, write down for yourself this same day, and know that today the king of Babylon has begun, in the region of Judea, to besiege Jerusalem and to wall it in with an army; and describe the siege itself by a parable and a proverb — which in the present place signifies a metaphor and transference — : Set on,' he says, 'a bronze pot, that is, a cauldron, and put water into it, and cut into pieces the whole body of the fattest animals, the thigh as well as the leg and the shoulder, and carefully separate the flesh from the bones and, once the flesh has been put into the cauldron, set, or arrange, the bones beneath the cauldron, and make piles and heaps of bones, so that the cooking of the cauldron may boil up not once but again and again, and the flesh may be boiled through within, and the bones beneath may be burned up by the fire.
Commentary on Ezekiel

It must also be noted how, from the beginning of the prophecy up to the present day when Jerusalem began to be besieged, the captivity comes in order. First the sword is called forth; then two ways are set out, Ammon and Jerusalem, and of these the lot falls for Nebuchadnezzar on the right-hand one; silver, bronze, tin, lead and iron are melted together in the city; the land too is not rained upon, but is overgrown with briers; afterwards, under the name of the two sisters Oholah and Oholibah, the sins of Samaria and Jerusalem are narrated, how the one has been captured and the other is to be captured; finally, in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, it is shown to Ezekiel, placed in captivity, and to those who were with him and had surrendered themselves with King Jeconiah, on what day the city began to be besieged, and the likeness of the cauldron is set forth so that, just as the flesh and the bones, heaped into the cauldron, are burned up by the fire, so the whole city is to perish together with its citizens, and none of those who were besieged is to remain without being consumed by famine, sword, pestilence, and the remaining part is to be led captive into Babylon. This same prophecy, however, can also pertain to the time of the Lord's passion, on account of which Jerusalem was surrounded by an army and her sons were slain and, when Titus the son of Vespasian besieged it, no one escaped to safety, and the temple suddenly, and, after fifty years, under Hadrian, the city was consumed by an everlasting fire. As for the present captivity, when Ezekiel was beholding these things in Babylon, and which Jeremiah sets at the beginning of his volume: What do you see, Jeremiah? And answering he said: A pot set alight, and its face from the face of the north, there are those who, according to tropology, transfer this whole passage to the consummation of the world, and who temper the ninth number, which in the holy Scriptures is the number of punishments and sorrows and always follows righteousness, by the clemency of the tenth month and the tenth day. For punishments are applied to the sick for this reason: that health may follow pain. The world, therefore, which is set in the evil one, is set alight by divine fire on the day of judgment; and the city of bloods is set upon coals of fire, so that what is written in Isaiah may be fulfilled: You have coals of fire, sit upon them: these will be a help to you. And this is difficult: how, when the coals and the bones are consumed — the bones of which even the Pharisees are full, to whom the Lord speaks in the Gospel: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, who are like whitewashed tombs, which within are full of filth and of the bones of the dead —, it is now said that the rust and filth of the world have not been consumed, but that even after the severity of judgment malice remains; this is easily resolved if we understand that saying of the Apostle: God has shut up all things under sin, that he may have mercy on all; for the creation was subjected to vanity. And the blood that has been poured out is set in the open sight of the whole creation, so that the crimes of all may be laid bare. But we can also take the most clear rock to be the Lord Savior, the rock which followed the people of Israel into the wilderness, of which it is written: They drank, moreover, from the rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ, because in him all things are revealed and what is written is fulfilled: Nothing is hidden that will not be revealed. And the Lord says that he will not have mercy, nor pass over the sins of the world, nor spare the impious nor be appeased, so that the ways of the impious may perish, according to what is set at the end of the first psalm: And the way of the impious will perish.
Commentary on Ezekiel

But do you wish, prophet, to know what this cauldron is, or what the flesh or the bones are? Speak these things, says the Lord: Woe to the city of bloods, that is, Jerusalem, to the cauldron whose rust, that is, malice, is excessive, and although fire has been put beneath it, yet its rust has not gone out of it; for even when captured and tortured they persevered in their former crime. Consume it part by part and one by one, so that no one remains to be saved. The lot has not fallen upon it, so that some should perish and others be saved, but a common destruction has come upon all; for its blood, that is, its murders and the slaughter of sons, is in the midst of it. This blood she poured out upon the most clear rock, so that it would be visible to all and not be covered with earth or with dust, so, namely, that my indignation might not pass by, but vengeance might hasten upon blood lying wholly in the open — for it is the way of nature that, if blood is poured out on the earth, the soil drinks up the moisture of the blood, or it is gradually covered with earth and dust; but when blood has been poured out upon a most clear rock which has no hollow, it slides and spreads over a wide space. And this indicates that she committed murders not hidden but public, according to what is said to Cain: The blood of your brother cries to me —.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Therefore say to the city of blood — of bloods not of one but of many —: Behold, I will make a great pyre in you, or I will bring a firebrand, which the common people call a titio [the everyday word for a firebrand], and I will set alight in you not only the soft and tender flesh but the hardest bones as well, and nothing shall remain in you that is not burned up by the fire.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And when both the flesh and the bones have been consumed and burned, set the empty cauldron itself upon the live coals, so that its bronze too may melt and be consumed and, the bronze being consumed, its rust too may perish; that is, when the city has been burned up by the fire, its malice may perish utterly with the city.
Commentary on Ezekiel

But what does it profit to have done what was commanded? Not even by fire could the rust and malice of the cauldron and of the city be taken away, and there remains in it a wicked and execrable uncleanness — for this is what 'zemma' signifies. And he makes an apostrophe to the cauldron itself, that is, to the city itself — : I wished to cleanse you, and you were not cleansed of your filth, nor will you be able to be cleansed any more until I fulfil my indignation upon you.
Commentary on Ezekiel

I the Lord have spoken, and my sentence cannot pass away. The siege of the city has already come; I will do what I have threatened, and I will not pass over — as I have often done — your crimes, and I will spare no longer, nor will I be appeased toward you even if you multiply your prayers, but I will repay you your ways and your devices; indeed, I will judge you according to your works and your thoughts, so that in this too I may show my clemency' — like a physician who does not spare rotten flesh, so that the healthy limbs may be saved: he does not spare in order to spare, he is cruel in order to have mercy, and he considers not the pain of the patient but the healing of the wound, according to that saying of the Gospel, preferring that one member should perish rather than that the whole body be killed —.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, behold, I am taking from you the desirable thing of your eyes with a stroke, and you shall not mourn nor weep, nor shall your tears flow. Groan in silence; you shall not make the mourning for the dead; let your crown be bound about you, and your shoes shall be on your feet, and you shall not veil your face with a mantle, nor eat the food of mourners. So I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening; and in the morning I did as he had commanded me. And the people said to me: Why do you not show us what these things mean that you are doing? And I said to them: The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Speak to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the pride of your dominion and the desirable thing of your eyes, and that over which your soul trembles. And your sons and daughters, whom you have left behind, shall fall by the sword. And you shall do as I have done: you shall not veil your faces with a mantle, and you shall not eat the food of mourners; you shall have crowns on your heads and shoes on your feet; you shall not mourn nor weep, but you shall waste away in your iniquities, and each shall groan to his brother. And Ezekiel shall be a portent to you: according to all that he has done you shall do, when this comes, and you shall know that I am the Lord God. And you, son of man, behold, on the day when I take from them their strength, and the joy of their dignity, and the desire of their eyes, on which their souls rest, their sons and their daughters; on that day, when one fleeing comes to you to announce it to you, on that day, I say, your mouth shall be opened with him who fled; and you shall speak and be silent no longer, and you shall be a portent to them, and you shall know that I am the Lord. (LXX: "And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, behold, I will take away from you the desirable things of your eyes in battle array (or in preparation); you shall not mourn nor weep, nor shall tears come to you. The groaning of the blood of the reins is mourning; your hair shall be bound up upon you and your shoes on your feet, nor shall you be comforted by their lips, and you shall not eat the bread of men. And I spoke to the people in the morning as he had commanded me, and my wife died in the evening; and in the morning I did as it was commanded me. And the people said to me: Will you not announce to us what these things are that you are doing? And I said to them: The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Say to the house of Israel: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I will defile my holy things, the pride of your strength, the desirable thing of your eyes, and the things which your souls spare. Your sons and your daughters, whom you have left behind, shall fall by the sword. And you shall do as I have done: you shall not be comforted by their mouth, and you shall not eat the bread of men, and your locks shall be upon your heads and your shoes on your feet; you shall not mourn nor weep, and you shall be consumed in your iniquities, and each shall comfort his brother. And Ezekiel shall be a portent to you: according to all that I have done you shall do, and when these things come, you shall know that I am Adonai the Lord. And you, son of man, will it not be on the day when I take away from them their strength, the exaltation of their glorying, the desirable things of their eyes, and the elation of their soul, their sons and their daughters; on that day he who has been saved will come to you, to announce it in your ears? On that day your mouth shall be opened to him who has fled; and you shall speak, and by no means be silent any longer, and you shall be a portent to them, and they shall know that I am the Lord.") Above, by the kindling of the pot and the cauldron, he had shown the siege of the city; now the prophetic word testifies that it has been captured and destroyed, and that the whole people has been either slain by the sword or led into captivity. And first, according to our custom, let us lay the foundations of the history. 'Son of man,' he says, 'behold, I will take away from the sight of your eyes whatever is desirable to you, and I will take it away 'with a stroke' — or, as the Seventy rendered, 'in preparation' —, so that, namely, you may prepare yourself not to do the things that are customarily done in mourning. You shall not mourn nor weep, nor shall flowing tears show the grief of your heart, but if perhaps you are overcome by excessive sorrow, keep your groaning silent, such as does not burst out into words'.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Let us come to the ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense], if only it does not seem forced to the prudence of a cautious reader. No one doubts that the son of man is said to be the Lord Savior, who at the last hour, that is, at the evening of this world, lost his former wife, and did not weep for her nor veil his face with a mantle nor receive any consolation from men, and who foretold in the morning the things to come which were fulfilled in the evening, and again in the morning, at his second coming, proved accomplished what he had foretold was to come: that the sanctuary of the Jews, and what they had held desirable in their eyes and that over which their souls trembled, had been profaned, and that their sons too and their daughters had fallen by the Roman sword. But what is said: You shall have a crown on your heads, and shoes shall be on your feet, we shall refer to this part: that they ought by no means to mourn nor to take up the signs of mourning, after they have received the truth in place of the shadow and certain of them have become Nazirites, and each one will be comforted over his brother, so that Ezekiel, whom God the Father strengthened, may be a portent to them, foretelling things to come; and that, after Jerusalem has been overthrown and the temple burned, and the whole world has heard this, and the dispersion of Israel, which inhabits the ends of the earth, then the words of the Lord, fulfilled in deed, may have freedom, and, his sanctuary having been profaned and the law fulfilled or destroyed according to the letter that kills, the glory of the Gospel may be laid open, and Israel may know that he himself is Lord and God, who foretold in the morning that these things would come, and proved by his coming that they were fulfilled in the evening and at the consummation of the world.
Commentary on Ezekiel

You shall not make the mourning for the dead (or, as the Seventy rendered: The groaning of the blood of the reins is mourning): by this he shows that his wife is going to die; for there follows immediately: And my wife died in the evening, which properly pertains to the union of the reins: nothing is more lovable to a man than a good wife, who is provided for a man by God, and to whom he is joined by the law of the Lord, and with whom he becomes one body. And what follows: Let your crown be bound about you, and your shoes shall be on your feet, signifies this: 'You shall have the hair which is shorn in mourning, and on your feet the shoes which mourners are accustomed to cast off' — whence David too, fleeing from his son Absalom and repenting over the murder of Uriah, walks with bare feet —. The Hebrews say: up to this day the Babylonian teachers, keeping the precepts of the law, bind the Decalogue, written on little parchments, around their heads, and these are the things that are commanded to hang before the eyes and on the forehead, so that they may always see what has been commanded; and because Ezekiel was a priest, he ought by no means to lay aside the crown of glorying, but to have it bound on his head. This is what they said. But let us, following the Seventy, understand by 'crown' the head of hair, although their translation too has by no means expressed the force of the Hebrew word. Nor shall you veil your face, he says, with a mantle, nor take the food of mourners: things which are customarily done in mourning, that people cover the face and receive from those who console them what the Greeks call περίδειπνα [funeral meals].
Commentary on Ezekiel

'I spoke,' he says, 'to the people the things the Lord had commanded me, and in the evening my wife died, the desirable thing of my eyes and the mourning of the loins and of the blood. And immediately, on the next day, in the morning, I did all the things that had been commanded me; and the people asked me why I had acted against the custom of all; and to those seeking the reasons for such great endurance I replied: The word of the Lord which came to me, that I should speak to the people of Israel, commanded these things: Behold, I (that is: now already) will profane my sanctuary, so that the temple may be burned and lie open to all foreigners and profane persons, the temple in which you had your pride, that is, your confidence and hope and the desire of your salvation, and at whose siege your souls were in dread; your sons too and your daughters, whom famine and pestilence had left remaining to you, I will consume with the sword, so that whatever I have done, you too may do'.
Commentary on Ezekiel

When custom is observed in mourning, the grief is moderate; but when so great a necessity of evils presses upon men that it is greater than all lamentation, each one, anxious about his own death, does not groan over the miseries of others, even though they are his nearest. 'You shall do nothing,' he says, 'of what is customarily done in mourning, but, when the city and the temple have been set on fire, you will be stunned at the magnitude of the evils; you will not cut your hair nor walk with bare feet, you will not mourn nor veil your faces with a mantle nor receive food from those who console you, but you will waste away, and you will be consumed in your iniquities, and you will scarcely have free groaning, lest you offend the pride of the victors if you are seen to weep publicly; so that Ezekiel the prophet may be a portent to you, and all that he did not do at the death of his wife, you may not do at the overthrow of the city and the temple'.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And yet more plainly: 'O son of man,' he says, 'at the time when I take away from them their strength — the confidence of the temple, as we have said —, and the joy of dignity and that in which they had their only hope, and the desire in which their souls rested, and besides their sons and their daughters — understood from the above: — I take away, at that time,' he says, 'when one fleeing from Jerusalem, or one who has escaped, comes to you, saying that the city has been overthrown, then you, who before had been silent and had no free groaning, and were of such great endurance that at the death of your wife and in the pain of your loins you did not shed a tear, will open your mouth and speak, not to him who has come but with him, so that whatever you had foretold was to come, he may announce as now accomplished; and you will no longer be silent, but you will rebuke them and say that all these things have befallen them deservedly, so that you may be a portent to them', according to what is written in Zechariah, that the prophets are men who portend, and the Lord says elsewhere: In the hands of the prophets I have been likened. Let this be said according to the history.

n: Ammon. These nations were punished five years after the Jews, chap. xxi. 19., and Jeremias xxvii. 3. (Calmet) --- "Egypt, Syria, Phœnicia, and Arabia," were conquered. (Berosus) --- Hast. God saw their dispositions, which they manifested afterwards. (Calmet) --- They rejoiced most, and were therefore punished with other nations. (Worthington)

East; the Chaldeans, (Sanctius) who conquered them, (Haydock) though the Scenite Arabs, who occupied the country after the inhabitants were removed, or the Armenians and Agarens, are rather meant than the Chaldeans. (Worthington)
Rabbath, the capital city of the Ammonites: it was afterwards called Philadelphia. (Challoner) --- Flocks. These constituted the riches of those Arabians.
Lord, and that it was not through impotence that my people became a prey. Ammon and Moab returned after some time, ver. 10., and chap. xvi. 53., and Jeremias xlix. 6.
Seir; Idumea. --- Nations, whose gods could not defend them. (Calmet) --- Thus they blasphemed the Lord. (Theodoret)
Shoulder; reduce to slavery, (Haydock) or take the strong places, (Jeremias xlviii. 7.; Calmet) or cities and strength of Moab. (Worthington)
With, or "like thee." Moab (ver. 11.) shall be treated like Ammon. (Haydock) --- Hebrew, "As for the," &c. (Calmet)
Revenge; exhorting the Chaldeans to destroy utterly, (Psalm cxxxvi. 7.) and seizing every opportunity of injuring the Jews, 2 Paralipomenon xxviii. 18., and Amos i. 11.

South. Hebrew, "Theman," a city at one extremity. The Chaldeans laid waste the country, (chap. xxxii. 29.) but did not remove the people, who seized the southern parts of Juda, till they were forced to submit to the Machabees.
Enmities. They also watched every moment to injure the Jews, Amos i. 5. But Nabuchodonosor was irritated, because they had assisted Tyre, Jeremias xlvii. 4.

Killers. Hebrew, "Ceretheans." David's guards were of this nation, 2 Kings viii. 18. They came originally from Crete; and the Septuagint have here, "Cretans;" (Calmet) as Grabe substitutes for "Judges of Sidon." (Haydock) --- Chaldean, "archers." --- Remnant. They deserve not the name of a nation, having been much reduced by Egypt and the Chaldeans. (Calmet)

f: Commentary on Ezekiel

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set (or make firm) your face against the Ammonites and you shall prophesy concerning them, and you shall say to the Ammonites: Hear the word of the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God: Because you said: Well done, well done, over my sanctuary (or because you rejoiced over my sanctuary) because it was profaned, and over the land of Israel because it was made desolate, and over the house of Judah because they were led into captivity, therefore I will hand you over to the sons of the east (or Cedem) as an inheritance; they shall set up their sheepfolds in you, and they shall pitch their tents in you; they themselves shall eat your fruits, and they themselves shall drink milk (or your richness). And I will make Rabbath a dwelling for camels (or the city of Ammon pastures for camels), and the Ammonites a lair for cattle, and you shall know that I am the Lord. For thus says the Lord God: Because you clapped with the hand, and struck (or stamped) with the foot, and rejoiced with all your feeling (or mocked from your soul) over the land of Israel, therefore behold, I will stretch out my hand over you, and I will hand you over for plunder to the nations, and I will slay you from among the peoples, and destroy from the lands, and crush, and you shall know that I am the Lord. When Jerusalem had been taken or besieged, after the one who had been able to escape came to Babylon and announced that the city was at any moment to be taken, or had been overthrown together with the temple, the prophetic discourse, according to the custom of all the prophets, turns against the other nations round about, which had mocked at the ruin of Jerusalem and the burning of the temple; and first against the Ammonites, who had a capital named Rabbath, which today is called Philadelphia after the king of Egypt Ptolemy, surnamed Philadelphus, who held Arabia together with Judea: 'Son' he says 'of man, set (or make firm) your face against the Ammonites, who were begotten of the stock of Lot, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God — for these are not the words of the prophet but of the Lord. Concerning the making firm of the face we have discussed more fully in this same prophet —: Because you said: Well done, well done, or, you mocked and rejoiced, because my temple and sanctuary was profaned by the entry of enemies, and over the land of Israel, because it was made desolate, and especially over the house of Judah, of the two tribes, which have now been led into captivity, therefore I too will hand you over to the sons of Cedem', whom we have translated 'eastern' — and no one doubts that the Midianites and the whole vast expanse of the desert lie next to the land of Arabia, who have herds of camels and multitudes of sheep and goats and live on this wealth —; which, as history relates in the book of Judges, also befell the land of Israel, when the Midianites came and grazed bare all their regions as far as Gaza. Μεταφορικῶς [metaphorically], then, Scripture signifies by way of the Midianites, the Ishmaelites and the Agarenes — who are now called Saracens, falsely taking to themselves the name of Sarah, so that, of course, they may seem to have been born of the free woman and mistress —; and it is said of King Nebuchadnezzar and all his army that he will come and take the city of Rabbath, which is called by this name either properly or because of its size — for 'Rabbath' means 'greatest' —; and so that we may not doubt that Nebuchadnezzar overthrew Arabia after Jerusalem was taken, Scripture testifies above: And you, son of man, set for yourself two ways, Ammon and Jerusalem, and the sword of the king of Babylon shall come, and again: At the head of the way of the city he shall cast. You shall set a way so that the sword may come to Rabbath of the Ammonites, and to Judah in most fortified Jerusalem, and again: Thus says the Lord God to the Ammonites and to their reproach. 'So the sons of Cedem will come and set up their sheepfolds like shepherds, and pitch tents; they themselves will lay waste your fruits and drink the milk and the richness of the land, once the flocks of camels and of all peoples have been let in, so that the Ammonites may be a lair for cattle', and by the compulsion of their misfortunes they may understand that he himself is the Lord, who both foretold the things to come and commanded that they should happen.
Commentary on Ezekiel

According to tropology we can understand the Ammonites — who were begotten of the seed of Lot in a cave, and begotten in drunkenness and incest — as all the heretics, of whom the apostle John also says: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would surely have remained with us; these have sprung from 'inclination' — for this is what 'Lot' is rendered in our language —, because: All have turned aside, together they have become useless; there is none who does good, there is not even one. Against these the prophet's face is set, or made firm, so that it may crush them by its severity, and it says to them: 'Because you mocked my Church in the time of persecution, and because my sanctuary had been profaned through various vices, whether by the vice of those who served me or by the cruelty of the enemies who persecuted my own, and because the land of Israel too, the senses that see God, was desolate of the choir of virtues, and because the sons of the house of Judah — the house that confesses the Lord, in which is the true faith and right confession — were led into captivity and ceased to serve the Lord, therefore you, who are all mockery, will be handed over to the sons of the east, who have set out from the true light, and you will be handed over as an inheritance, so that you too may learn to confess the Lord'. And by metaphor it is said that the sons of the east set their sheepfolds over them and pitch tents and drink milk and eat fruits, and that the city once of pride becomes a dwelling for camels, which, having laid down the burden of sins, can enter through the eye of a needle, and a lair for cattle, which are ruled by the good shepherd, so that, when they have done this, mingled with and handed over to the shepherds of the east, they may understand that he himself is the Lord.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Nor was it enough for the Ammonites to mock and say 'Well done, well done' over the temple and sanctuary of the Lord, which had been profaned by the entry of various nations; but so great was the wantonness of their mocking that the whole people together clattered with hands and feet and shouted with all the passion of the heart, because the land of Israel was desolate. Therefore not through angels nor through other ministries, but the Lord himself, stretching out his hand to strike, will hand it over for plunder — not at all to camels and flocks of sheep but, more plainly, to the nations — so that it may be utterly uprooted from the number of the peoples, and perish, and be brought to nothing; and after it has been crushed, then it may understand that he himself is the Lord, who judges all things and has power over all lands.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And again he reproaches them for having mocked with excessive passion of heart at the ruins of the people of God, and for having thought the land of Israel utterly deserted, for which they deserve the hand of the avenging God, so that those who had exceeded the measure of exultation and joy over the ruin of the house of Judah are not handed over to the sons of the east at all, but become a plunder for all the nations, and are slain from among the peoples, and perish, and are crushed, and are to be believed to belong not at all to the stock of Abraham but to all the nations; and then, by the greatness of their misfortunes and by their own crushing and the slaughter of their people, they may know that he himself is the Lord. What we have understood generally of the Church can be understood of each one of the saints, at whose ruin the men of the world rejoice, and the adverse powers too, if they have lost a chastity of long standing, since the wicked think it a consolation for their own crimes if they have many partners in crimes and in punishment; and no one does this unless he is a son of Ammon, that is, a son of the people, who was begotten in declination.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Thus says the Lord God: Because Moab and Seir said: Behold, the house of Judah is like all the nations, therefore behold, I will open the shoulder of Moab, from its cities, I say, and from its borders, the glorious places of the land, Bethiesimoth and Beelmeon and Cariathaim, to the sons of the east together with the Ammonites; and I will give it as an inheritance, so that there may be no more remembrance of the Ammonites among the nations. And upon Moab I will execute judgments, and they shall know that I am the Lord. (LXX: "Thus says Adonai the Lord: Because Moab ※ and Seir ⁚ said: Behold, the house of Judah is like all the nations, therefore behold, I will loosen the shoulder of Moab from the cities of its promontories, the chosen land, the house of Bethiesimuth above the spring of the maritime city, the sons of the east over the Ammonites; I have given it to him as an inheritance, so that there may be no remembrance of the Ammonites among the nations. And upon Moab I will execute vengeances, and they shall know that I am the Lord." What we have translated 'and Seir' is not found in the Seventy but has been added from Theodotion.) In this place, however, the Hebrews tell a ridiculous tale: after the city was opened and the temple unbarred, and the sons of Ammon and Moab and Seir had entered the temple and seen the Cherubim protecting the mercy seat, they said: 'As all the nations worship images, so Judah too has idols of its religion'; and for this reason, they say, the Lord was angered and handed them over to captivity. We, however, say this: that these too mocked the house of Judah when it was taken by the Chaldeans, thinking that, as there had been no help from God among the other nations, so too the kingdom of Judah and Jerusalem, bereft of God's protection, had lain open to the power of Babylon.
Commentary on Ezekiel

But to this day 'Moab', which means 'from the father', and 'Seir', which is rendered 'hairy' and 'shaggy', looks down on and despises the house of Judah, in which is the true confession, and thinks that it can be overthrown as easily as the fortifications of the other cities are overthrown.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Therefore, not a long time afterward but at the present moment, the Lord threatens that he will loosen, or open, the shoulder of Moab — that is, its strength and might — from its cities, so that the Babylonian conqueror may enter in to them too, and the cities in Moab may cease to be, and in its borders and boundaries the glorious cities may be destroyed whose names he sets down: 'Bethiesimoth and Beelmeon and Cariathaim', for which the Seventy, intending I know not what, translated 'the house of Bethiesimuth', although this word signifies 'a deserted village', while 'Beelmeon' too is to this day a very large village in Moab, which they rendered 'above the spring', and 'Cariathaim' 'a maritime city'; and it too is handed over, together with the Ammonites, to the sons of the east, namely the Babylonians, according to the sense which we have expounded against the Ammonites. 'And I will give,' he says, 'Moab as an inheritance, so that, as there is no more remembrance of the Ammonites among the nations, so also upon Moab I will execute vengeances and judgments, and they may know that I am the Lord, who handed Judah over for sin and stand forth as avenger against the Ammonites and against Moab'.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Hence the Lord threatens that he will open, or loosen, all the strength of the Moabites, so that they may cease to have cities and may no longer trust in the dialectical art, but that all its boundaries, which he calls promontories because of the dashing of the waves, may be destroyed, and that the glorious and chosen lands — 'Bethiesimoth', which means 'house of solitude' and 'deserted', and 'Beelmeon', which is likewise rendered 'having a spring' or 'above the spring', and 'Cariathaim', which the Seventy translated 'a maritime city' — may perish; for although they have the strength of fighters, and the glorious go forth to battle with the art of fighting, and advance hedged about and fortified on every side, yet their glorious land is not a house of habitation but a house of solitude; and though they think that they have a spring of knowledge and a maritime city that can withstand all the storms of the world, promising themselves endurance and strength, yet they will be turned to this end, that they too may be handed over to the sons of the east of the true light in Christ, just as the Ammonites were handed over, who trusted in their heretical multitude. And let us consider the benefit, and the clemency of God in the very threat: that they are handed over together with the Ammonites to the sons of the east as an inheritance, and that no heresy at all may be named among the nations, but that, judgments and vengeances having been executed upon Moab for its arrogance, they may know by the outcome of things that it is the Lord who orders all things.
